newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 1.9 billion yuan from 1.6 billion yuan last Friday with the 60-day contract the most active.
Traders said some non-bank financial institutions did more business through the short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank, pushing up the volume.

"Non-bank financial institutions traded more today, adding some liquidity to the market," said one trader. "But most state-run banks were cautious about trading ahead of a national meeting of financial institutions."
Senior officials of the central bank and other financial institutions will meet in Beijing next week for a national policy conference, officials said on Monday.
Traders said they expected the meeting to re-affirm a continued tight monetary policy in force since 1993.
This was likely to help stabilise the interbank market rates in the short term despites ample short-term money supply at the national level, they said.
The rates are likely to move around the current level in the next few trading days in slow trading with major banks staying on the sidelines, they said.
